ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of every shareholder holding 25% or more, director, manager, and authorized signatory against: (i) consolidated UN Security Council sanctions lists; (ii) the US OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons (SDN) list; (iii) the EU consolidated financial sanctions list; (iv) Egyptian EMLCU and Public Prosecutor anti-terrorism lists issued under Law No. 80 of 2002; (v) the Central Bank of Egypt watchlist; and (vi) Interpol Red Notices. Politically Exposed Persons, whether domestic or foreign, automatically trigger enhanced due diligence requiring source-of-wealth and source-of-funds evidence, senior-management approval, and enhanced ongoing monitoring for documentary LC and SWIFT TT payment rails, in accordance with FATF Recommendations 10, 12, and 24. All UBO and KYC results must be documented and retained for at least five years after the end of the business relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: GAFI Online Company Establishment and Licensing Portal operated by the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) at www.gafi.gov.eg, integrated with the Unified Commercial Register of the Ministry of Supply and Internal Trade; name clearance is processed through the GAFI One-Stop-Shop for Limited Liability Companies.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name must be stated in official Arabic script as the primary registered name; a Latin-script English transliteration may be recorded in the parallel commercial-register data field. The Arabic name governs before Egyptian courts and registries. The name must be distinctive and must not be identical or misleadingly similar to any existing registered trade name. Transliteration must follow the GAFI-approved naming and lettering convention, and the entity-type suffix 'LLC' or its Arabic equivalent must be included where required under Law No. 159 of 1981.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank, banking, or financial intermediary (Central Bank of Egypt prior approval required)
Insurance or reinsurance (Financial Regulatory Authority prior approval required)
Securities, brokerage, funds, or asset management (Financial Regulatory Authority prior approval required)
Petroleum, oil, or gas (Ministry of Petroleum and Mineral Resources prior approval required)
Military, armed forces, or defense (Ministry of Defense prior approval required)
Nuclear or radioactive (competent nuclear regulatory authority prior approval required)
National, republic, sovereign, government, or state (reserved to state entities or GAFI discretion)
Islamic or religious references capable of misleading, where such use requires GAFI consultation with religious-affairs authorities
Words implying a statutory license, chamber, union, or certification for activities not yet licensed within the ISIC 4669 scrap-consignment scope
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 15 working days of a rejection notice, the applicant's Egyptian Bar-registered counsel may file an administrative objection at the GAFI One-Stop-Shop, attaching the rejection slip, a revised Arabic name, and a legal memorandum. The GAFI Name Clearance Committee must issue a decision within 10 working days. A further adverse decision may be appealed to the Egyptian Council of State (Administrative Court) within 60 days. If the name reservation is due to expire while an appeal is pending, the applicant may submit a written extension request for an additional 30 days accompanied by proof of pending incorporation steps and payment of the GAFI extension fee.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditionally accepted. GAFI permits a service-provider or virtual address to be recorded as the initial registered seat in the memorandum of association. However, the Commercial Registry and the customs and General Organization for Export and Import Control licensing framework for non-ferrous scrap consignment expect a substantive physical office or warehouse in the Governorate where operations are conducted. Egyptian banks generally require a verifiable physical address for documentary LC and SWIFT TT account opening and may reject a purely virtual registered office. The physical address must be updated with GAFI and the Commercial Registry at the latest upon commencement of operations.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High: approximately 80% likelihood of at least one unannounced compliance inspection in the first 12 months, reflecting the medium-risk-enhanced AML tier applicable to recyclable non-ferrous metal trading. Inspections may be jointly performed by GAFI compliance officers, Commercial Registry inspectors, and supply, customs, and administrative-control authorities at the declared operating address.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Egyptian Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 (as amended by Law No. 148 of 2020 and Investment Law No. 72 of 2017), Articles 1-10 and 26 covering the formation, share capital and management of a Limited Liability Company; Executive Regulations issued by the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) – Companies Registration Department, Cairo, Egypt
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Memorandum of Association and Articles of Association (Aqd Al-Ta'sis wa Nizam Al-Qa'idah), submitted through the GAFI online one-stop shop as the incorporation application
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for an Egyptian LLC; share capital is set by the partners in the Memorandum of Association and must be fully subscribed. Share capital is paid into a bank account upon incorporation when required by GAFI or when the activity involves import/export; a separate escrow account is not mandatory for LLCs under Companies Law.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) The Subscription of Shares set out in the signed Memorandum of Association is hereby ratified and accepted. (2) The registered office of the Company at [address, Cairo/Giza, Egypt] is adopted as the official seat for service of process and correspondence. (3) [Name], [Name], and [Name] are appointed as First Managers, each with authority to act jointly in executing banking, commercial, and licensing filings. (4) The managers are authorized to open bank accounts, appoint counsel, and take all necessary actions to obtain incorporation certificates, commercial registration, tax cards, and environmental licenses. (5) Said appointments take effect upon the issuance of the Company certificate of incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log into the GAFI e-services platform and submit three proposed Arabic trade names for the LLC. Pay the name reservation fee and indicate the intended activity of wholesale of recycled non-ferrous scrap and copper wire. Receive the name reservation certificate, which is valid for 60 days. The name must not conflict with existing registered trademarks or government bodies.
required_dossiers: Passport copies of all proposed managers and shareholders
Notarized power of attorney for the local agent or law firm, if any
Proof of payment of name reservation fees
Preliminary approval letter from GAFI if the name includes sensitive words or foreign references
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is rejected, file an administrative reconsideration request with GAFI's Name Committee within 15 days or submit a revised list of names through the same portal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public Office (Shehar Al-Tawthiq) or GAFI-authorized notary at the one-stop shop
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the LLC Memorandum of Association and Articles of Association in Arabic in accordance with Companies Law No. 159 of 1981. All partners or their authorized representatives must attend before the notary to verify identities and sign the founding documents. Notarize the signatures and seal the document, which then becomes the foundational instrument for incorporation.
required_dossiers: Draft Memorandum and Articles of Association (Arabic)
Valid passports and national IDs of all partners and managers
Name reservation certificate from GAFI
Notarized power of attorney for signatories, if applicable
Statement of non-disqualification for handling commercial activities
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary objects to any clause, correct the capital, share allocation, or activity description and re-submit for notarization; additional notarial fees may apply.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: GAFI Incorporation Filing and Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI Companies Registration Department, Cairo One-Stop Shop (also through electronic upload)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarized founding documents, name certificate, and supporting dossiers to GAFI for legal review and company registration. Pay the applicable incorporation, registration, and publication fees. If the company pursues foreign trade or import/export, provide the additional import/export filing details. GAFI will issue the formal Certificate of Incorporation and a data file for the commercial registry.
required_dossiers: Notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association
Name reservation certificate
Registered office lease contract or title deed (notarized)
First Board Resolution appointing managers
Signed written consents of managers to act as managing directors
Bank certificate of capital payment if capital is paid in cash
GAFI-specific incorporation application form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to any GAFI queries or comments within 30 calendar days by filing amended documents, additional signatures, or clarifications. If the application is challenged, appeal to the GAFI Investment Complaints Committee for a binding administrative resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Registration and Tax Card Issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registry Office (Ministry of Trade and Industry) and Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) Central Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Take the issued Certificate of Incorporation to the competent Commercial Registry office to register the LLC in the commercial register and obtain a commercial registration certificate. Then apply to the ETA within 45 days to obtain a Tax Identification Number (TIN) and an income tax card. Complete Form 1 for tax registration, specifying the activity code matching ISIC 4669 wholesale of waste and scrap.
required_dossiers: GAFI Certificate of Incorporation
Notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association
Commercial lease contract for storage/sorting facility
Manager IDs and passport copies
Signed board resolution designating tax representatives
Proof of official record fee deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Commercial Registry queries the registered office or activity, re-file with corrected supporting documents. If ETA rejects the tax card, appeal to the Tax Authority's Internal Review and submit corrected address or capital evidence.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Al-Jaridah Al-Rasmiyah (Official Gazette), Cabinet of Ministers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a summary of the LLC formation, including the registered office, capital, partners, and managers, for publication in the Official Gazette. Pay the publication fee and obtain the official publication receipt. This makes the formation legally effective against third parties and is the final mandatory step for corporate existence.
required_dossiers: GAFI Certificate of Incorporation
Notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association
Commercial registration certificate
Publication request form from GAFI
Evidence of paid publication fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Gazette requests amendments, correct typographical errors and re-submit the publication request; obtain a stabilization letter confirming the final publication date.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Environment – Waste Management Regulatory Authority (WMRA); and for consignment/import-export operations, the General Organization for Export and Import Control (GOEIC) under the Ministry of Trade and Industry
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Licence for Trading and Consignment of Non-Hazardous Recycled Scrap (Non-Ferrous Metals and Copper Wire) – Category: Commercial Storage and Wholesale Distribution

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency (EEAA), Ministry of Environment
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Type B (Light Impact) – Registration with an Environmental Compliance Certificate (ECC) required for storage, sorting, and physical transfer of non-hazardous scrap; a full EIA report is not required unless the operation includes shredding, heat treatment, or chemical processing.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with Law No. 4/1994 (as amended) and Waste Management Law No. 202/2020. Treated wastewater discharge to municipal sewers must not exceed BOD 60 mg/L, TSS 80 mg/L, and oil/grease 10 mg/L. No open burning or VOC emissions exceeding EEAA limits; particulate emissions from storage areas must remain below 50 mg/m³ at any exhaust point. All waste transfer must be documented using approved manifest forms and only to licensed recycling facilities.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety clearance certificate from the Civil Defense Authority after inspection of storage racks, fire extinguishers, and emergency egress; structural load inspection certificate from the local Governorate engineering department; and an occupational health and workplace clearance from the Ministry of Manpower covering manual handling, personal protective equipment, and dust/fume hygiene.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) of the Ministry of Finance; official unified tax services and electronic invoicing portals at https://www.eta.gov.eg and https://einvoice.gov.eg.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned Egyptian LLC must: (1) incorporate through the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) one-stop shop and obtain commercial registration; (2) apply to the ETA for a Tax Card, which generates the statutory Tax Identification Number (TIN), submitting the incorporation contract, notarized power of attorney, commercial register extract, lease/activity certificate, and manager appointment deed; (3) register for VAT under Law No. 67 of 2016 once taxable annual turnover exceeds EGP 500,000, or earlier on a voluntary basis, obtaining a separate VAT code; (4) activate the ETA e-invoicing account by obtaining an approved electronic signature and completing API client onboarding from the ETA sandbox to the production gateway. A non-resident seller without an onshore entity must appoint a tax representative, register a permanent establishment, and obtain a TIN before issuing Egyptian invoices.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; an Egyptian LLC is a separate legal taxpayer subject to corporate income tax at the standard headliner rate of 22.5%; resident-managed LLCs are assessed on worldwide income, while non-resident owners and PEs are assessed on Egyptian-source income only. The LLC has no fiscal transparency or pass-through status, and purely exporting activities remain corporate-taxable unless specific Suez Canal Economic Zone or new-investment incentives apply.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Egyptian law does not provide a US-style check-the-box or hybrid mismatch election for LLCs. Available statutory elections include: voluntary VAT registration under Law 67/2016 before reaching the mandatory EGP 500,000 threshold; the simplified/presumptive tax regime for micro and small enterprises under Law 152 of 2020, subject to turnover limits; and the choice of eligible free-zone investment incentives under Egypt's Investment Law, where approved by GAFI, which may alter effective direct tax exposure but not LLC entity-level character.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under Law No. 67 of 2016, as amended, administered under the Unified Tax Procedures Law No. 90 of 2022.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500,000 of annual taxable supplies; mandatory VAT registration applies to any person whose taxable turnover exceeds this threshold, with voluntary registration permitted below it; registration is also mandatory for taxable importers.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All VAT-registered taxpayers are phased into mandatory ETA e-invoicing. The issuer must transmit invoices to the ETA API gateway in JSON/XML in real time, signed with the taxpayer's approved electronic signature; the ETA performs schema, duplication, and fiscal-validation checks and returns a unique invoice identifier, a digital stamp, and a QR code. B2C cashier receipts are separately covered by the e-receipts mandate. Invoices not cleared or not integrated are treated as fiscally unissued, with consequent denial of input VAT deduction and fixed penalties.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A zero rate applies to goods physically exported from Egypt, provided the seller is VAT-registered, the goods are dispatched under a valid customs export declaration (Bayan), title and risk pass to a non-resident buyer, the export is completed within the permitted period, and the value is received in convertible foreign currency through an authorized Egyptian bank. Related input VAT may be refunded on substantiation. Services rendered to a non-resident and consumed outside Egypt may also be zero-rated when properly evidenced. Any applicable state restrictions or permits for recycled scrap exports must be complied with in parallel to tax treatment.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Bayan) and Egypt Single Administrative Document
Bill of Lading or Master Air Waybill
Inward Remittance Certificate or credited foreign-currency bank advice
Signed commercial invoice and packing list
Statutory scrap export license or GOEIC compliance certificate, if applicable
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The ETA cross-matches e-invoices, customs export declarations, shipping records, and bank FX receipts; a zero-rating claim is retrospectively denied if the documentary bundle is incomplete, the goods are not proved to have left Egypt, or export proceeds are not repatriated through the banking system within 180 days from shipment (absent an approved extension), at which point VAT at 14% becomes payable with delay penalties. Deliberate false export claims constitute tax evasion under Law 67/2016 and the Unified Tax Procedures Law, carrying monthly delay fines, additional penalties of up to 100-200% of the evaded tax, criminal sanctions including imprisonment, and a five-year or longer reassessment window in fraud cases.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Egyptian pound operates under a managed-float regime with current account convertibility for valid trade transactions routed through authorized banks. Capital account transactions, including direct equity inflows, foreign financing, and profit repatriation, remain subject to CBE authorization, documentary verification, and tax clearance. Profit remittance requires audited financial statements, a valid tax card, and confirmation that all Egyptian tax liabilities have been settled. Temporary FX liquidity narrowing can result in discretionary allocation or queuing for outward remittances; therefore trade flows must use documented underlying merchandise and supported payment purposes to obtain priority.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Egyptian exporters must repatriate full export proceeds to a CBE-licensed bank within 180 days from the Bill of Lading date, unless a shorter period is prescribed by commodity-specific CBE circulars. The proceeds must be deposited in the exporter's foreign-currency account at an authorized Egyptian bank; conversion to Egyptian pounds is optional unless the CBE imposes a temporary full or partial surrender requirement during acute currency shortages. Failure to meet the repatriation timeline triggers fines, suspension of export financing facilities, and denial of subsequent usance LC facilities.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore electronic money institution (EMI) licenses are not recognized by the CBE. A foreign fintech cannot provide domestic Egyptian IBANs or clear trade settlements without obtaining a local payments license and entering a sponsor-bank arrangement with an Egyptian licensed bank. For documentary trade, a CBE-authorized commercial bank conduit is legally mandatory; offshore virtual IBANs would be rejected for customs and CBE FX registration.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Authorized signatories, general managers, and ultimate beneficial owners are generally required to undergo an in-person identity verification interview at an Egyptian branch. Remote opening is not accepted for a corporate account dedicated to non-ferrous scrap trade because of the enhanced AML risk profile. After the physical meeting, supplementary documents may be submitted digitally, but the account activation is conditional upon successful original-document inspection at the designated branch.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Independent high-net-worth UBO with previous regulatory sanctions in another jurisdiction
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial Registry extract, certified certificate of incumbency, passport of each UBO, Emirates/N/NY? resident jurisdiction court-clearance certificate, sworn declaration of source of wealth and source of funds, board resolution approving the Egypt account, and a current tax clearance certificate from the jurisdiction of tax residence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk arms-length buyer located in a jurisdiction perceived as scrap-metal diversion hub
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Compliance due-diligence report on the buyer, audited financial statements or confirmed bank reference, transaction chain contracts, Egyptian Customs export declaration and unique electronic barcode, third-party inspection certificate, original ocean Bill of Lading, and an end-consumer undertaking affirming recycling use.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of a seller that does not possess an Egyptian ministry-issued scrap trading license
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Seller's full statutory trade license, environmental permit, police-issued metal dealer registration, certified supplier KYC package, original purchase invoices and delivery waybills, scale receipts, and an attestation from the local district administration confirming lawful collection and transport.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between copper weight/value declared at customs and underlying supplier invoices
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified weighbridge tickets, sealed container tally sheets, Customs Goods Value Number (GVN) receipt, tax-inspected invoice set, warehouse storage lease, and reconciliation letter from the certified public accountant corroborating contract shipment quantities.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Foreign investment capital must be wired via SWIFT MT103 or MT202 into the LLC's EGP-denominated or USD-denominated account at an Egyptian licensed bank. The remittance instruction must use a valid CBE purpose code such as 1000 for foreign direct investment in the non-financial sector or 6311 for payment for exported industrial goods. The recipient must hold a GAFI investor certificate and submit a copy of the remittance confirmation with the underlying share subscription agreement. The receiving bank will file a CBE foreign-trade declaration, and funds are credited only after clearance of sanctions and regulatory filters. To avoid reduced credit from correspondent deductions, remitters should instruct payment charges as OUR with a separate reimbursement arrangement.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade disbursements for physical scrap copper exports are cleared through the documentary LC system: the buyer opens a sight or usance LC through a CBE-licensed confirming bank. Disbursement is triggered after the negotiating bank presents the full set of compliant transport documents—clean on-board Bill of Lading, commercial invoice, packing list, certificate of origin, and any third-party quality certificate—through SWIFT MT7xx messages. Direct bank-to-bank payments via SWIFT MT103 are reserved for premium adjustments exceeding the documentary threshold, and must be tied to the same underlying commercial invoice to avoid rejection by the receiving bank. All outward transfers rely on CBE's e-registration portal and the Integrated Customs System.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: CBE-approved full-delivery FX forward contracts up to 180 days backed by authenticated trade documentation
FX swaps between EGP and USD arranged through an authorized Egyptian dealer
Cross-currency swaps linked to the EGP for project-level funding without speculative leverage
Commodity price hedging with copper swaps or forward contracts approved by the CBE for non-financial end-user exporters

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Form No. 19)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before April 30 following the fiscal year ending December 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of EGP 500 per month; monthly delay interest at 1.5% on unpaid tax; continued failure triggers administrative assessment and enforcement collection.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registry Office under the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Renew during January of each calendar year for the preceding year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal penalty of EGP 500 per month; suspension of commercial registration, restriction from trade, and risk of administrative strike-off after 6 months of continued non-renewal.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due by March 31 for the preceding calendar year contribution list
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monthly increment penalty of 2% on unpaid contributions; employer prosecution and issuance of executive collection order; director personal liability in sustained non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Financial Information Unit (FIU) and Commercial Registry, where designated
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after the fiscal year end; UBO register must be filed annually
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative monetary fine under AML law up to EGP 200,000; additional penalties for providing false UBO information; potential restriction of bank transactions and share transfers.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Tax Card Renewal / Governorate Trade License Annual Update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority and the relevant Local Governorate
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Rolling annual renewal before the expiry date of the issued tax card or trade license
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Imposition of late fee of EGP 300 plus administrative penalties; failure to renew can suspend import/export privileges and open a port to tax inspection and penalty assessment.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A mandatory statutory audit is required where the LLC has paid-in capital exceeding EGP 500,000, or annual net turnover exceeding EGP 10,000,000, or total assets exceeding EGP 5,000,000; otherwise an accountant certified under Egyptian law must review and sign the financial statements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS) as issued by the Egyptian Financial Regulatory Authority; entities qualifying as 'larger' may apply full IFRS, while SMEs may use the simplified EAS for small enterprises.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The LLC must maintain a current register of ultimate beneficial owners and submit an annual confirmation to the FIU/Commercial Registry within 30 days of fiscal year end. Any shareholding transfer changing beneficial ownership must be reported and registered with the Commercial Registry within 15 days of the transaction; failure to update invalidates corporate accounts and invites AML sanctions.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 22.5% of taxable profits for Egyptian resident companies and Egyptian permanent establishments of non-resident enterprises.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Egypt generally has no broad corporate tax holiday for an ordinary LLC conducting recycled scrap-metal trading. Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 and special-zone regimes may provide reduced rates, tax holidays, or other incentives only where the company, project, location, and approvals satisfy the applicable investment or zone legislation. Qualifying listed-share dividend income may receive a reduced dividend tax rate. Taxable profit is computed after permitted deductions, depreciation, and other statutory adjustments. Losses may generally be carried forward for five years; carryback is generally unavailable.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual corporate income tax return for legal persons, commonly referred to as Egyptian Tax Authority Form 29, filed electronically through the Egyptian Tax Authority electronic tax return portal. Electronic filing and payment obligations apply to taxpayers within the relevant ETA implementation scope.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual return is generally due within four months after the end of the financial year. For a calendar-year company ending on 31 December, the ordinary deadline is 30 April of the following year. A company using an approved non-calendar financial year follows the corresponding four-month rule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, commercial registration details, tax registration number, VAT registration number where applicable, registered address, legal form, principal business activity, and contact details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident enterprise files through its Egyptian permanent establishment or taxable presence and must identify the Egyptian branch, project office, agent, or other taxable nexus. A non-resident without an Egyptian taxable presence generally does not file a resident-company return solely because it receives Egyptian-source income, but Egyptian withholding and reporting obligations may apply.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Financial-year start and end dates, original or amended return status, and relevant accounting basis.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the approved Egyptian branch or permanent-establishment accounting period. Disclose any change of accounting period and retain approval or supporting evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Profit or loss shown in the statutory financial statements before Egyptian corporate income tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A branch or permanent establishment must prepare an attributable profit computation supported by functional analysis, books, contracts, and records for Egyptian activities.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income excluded or exempt under Egyptian law, with legal basis and supporting schedules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not exclude foreign-source or treaty-protected income without documenting the applicable treaty article, residence evidence, beneficial ownership, and Egyptian-source-income analysis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-backs for expenses not incurred for business purposes, unsupported expenses, prohibited provisions, non-deductible taxes, penalties, and other statutory adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenses allocated to an Egyptian permanent establishment must satisfy the arm's-length and direct-business-purpose requirements. Head-office allocations require reliable allocation keys and supporting documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax depreciation and statutory capital allowance adjustments for machinery, equipment, vehicles, warehouses, and other business assets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use Egyptian tax depreciation rules rather than automatically adopting financial-statement depreciation. Maintain acquisition invoices, customs documents, capitalization records, and asset registers.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Inventory and cost of goods sold
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Opening inventory, purchases, freight, customs charges, processing costs, closing inventory, and cost of recycled copper and other scrap sold.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile quantities and values to purchase contracts, weighbridge records, shipping documents, import declarations, export records, warehouse records, and bank payments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Adjustments arising from transfer-pricing analysis, including purchases, sales, financing, services, royalties, guarantees, and management charges.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the arm's-length principle and disclose transactions with foreign related parties or associated enterprises. Maintain transaction-level data and supporting transfer-pricing documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Current-year loss, brought-forward losses, utilized losses, and remaining loss balance, subject to the five-year carryforward limitation and statutory restrictions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A permanent establishment must separately track losses attributable to its Egyptian activities. Do not use losses generated by another legal entity or by non-Egyptian activities without a specific legal basis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income after statutory additions, deductions, depreciation, exempt-income adjustments, transfer-pricing adjustments, and permitted loss utilization.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile the taxable-profit computation to the financial statements and retain a clear bridge from accounting profit to Egyptian taxable profit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable profit multiplied by the applicable rate, less permitted credits, payments on account, and withholding tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim Egyptian withholding tax credits only where supported by official certificates or legally acceptable evidence and where the corresponding income is included in the Egyptian tax base.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Advance payments, withholding tax credits, previous payments, balance payable, refund claim, and payment reference.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Pay through approved Egyptian banking or electronic payment channels and retain payment confirmations. A refund position may be subject to review and supporting-document requests.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Financial statements, tax reconciliation, depreciation schedule, inventory schedules, related-party schedules, withholding certificates, and other documents requested by the ETA.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide Arabic translations or certified translations when required and preserve original contracts, invoices, customs records, shipping files, and tax-residence documents.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file, late filing, inaccurate filing, failure to keep records, and failure to pay may trigger administrative fines under Tax Procedures Law No. 206 of 2020, additional tax for late payment calculated by statutory monthly rules, assessment of omitted tax, and interest or equivalent statutory charges. Repeated or material non-compliance can increase penalties. There is generally no separate daily surcharge; late-payment additional tax is ordinarily calculated by reference to each month or part of a month under the applicable law. Tax evasion may trigger criminal penalties, including imprisonment and fines.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Egyptian Tax Authority electronic withholding-tax declarations and payment systems for tax withheld on specified payments, including payments to non-residents, employment-related payments, and other legally designated categories.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Monthly or according to the applicable withholding-tax reporting cycle
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The withholding agent must deduct tax at the time required by law, remit it within the statutory period, and submit the required declaration and certificates. The exact deadline depends on the payment category and current ETA procedures.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Egyptian tax number, legal name, address, period, and declaration type.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Egyptian payer or Egyptian permanent establishment generally acts as withholding agent for Egyptian-source payments to a non-resident.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Name, country of residence, tax identification number where available, beneficial-owner status, and payment details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Obtain a current certificate of tax residence before applying treaty relief and verify that the payee is the beneficial owner where required.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Dividend, interest, royalty, service fee, management fee, commission, lease payment, or other payment category.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Classify by substance and contract terms. Do not relabel royalties, interest, or services as a tax-exempt purchase price.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross amount, domestic statutory rate, treaty rate if validly claimed, tax withheld, and currency conversion.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply domestic rates unless treaty documentation and procedural conditions are satisfied. Retain calculations and exchange-rate evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Payment date, tax remittance date, payment reference, and withholding certificate issued to the payee.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Issue the required certificate and retain proof of remittance for treaty relief, foreign tax credit, audit, and beneficial-owner review.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to withhold or remit may make the payer liable for the tax that should have been withheld, additional tax, administrative penalties, and potentially criminal consequences where conduct constitutes tax evasion, concealment, falsification, or deliberate non-compliance.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: Dividends distributed by an Egyptian resident company are generally subject to a 10% dividend withholding or dividend-distribution tax. The rate may be reduced to 5% for qualifying dividends from listed shares where the statutory ownership and holding-period conditions are satisfied. Treaty rates may further reduce the Egyptian rate, subject to treaty entitlement, residence certification, beneficial ownership, and procedural compliance.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, obtain a valid certificate of tax residence from the recipient's foreign tax authority, verify treaty residence and beneficial ownership, analyze the relevant dividend, interest, royalty, or business-profits article, confirm any minimum ownership and holding-period condition, and retain contracts, corporate documents, payment evidence, and substance records. The Egyptian payer should apply the treaty rate only where the applicable Egyptian administrative requirements are met; otherwise it should withhold at the domestic rate and the recipient may pursue the available refund or relief procedure with the ETA. Treaty relief is not available for conduit arrangements, artificial structures, or unsupported beneficial-owner claims.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Payments of Egyptian-source interest and royalties to non-residents are generally subject to 20% withholding tax under domestic law, subject to applicable exemptions and treaty limitations. A treaty may reduce the rate, commonly to a negotiated ceiling that varies by treaty and payment type. Service fees, management fees, commissions, and other payments require separate source and permanent-establishment analysis; a 20% rate should not be applied automatically to every cross-border payment. Documentary evidence, residence certificates, beneficial-ownership analysis, and correct payment classification are required before applying treaty relief.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Egyptian transfer-pricing rules generally require local-file and master-file documentation where related-party transactions exceed EGP 8,000,000 for the relevant transaction category or otherwise fall within the applicable documentation requirements. A country-by-country report generally applies to an ultimate parent or surrogate parent in the relevant jurisdiction where consolidated group revenue reaches the statutory threshold, commonly EGP 3,000,000,000 or its prescribed equivalent under current Egyptian rules. Thresholds, filing formats, and submission timing must be checked against current ETA instructions for the relevant fiscal year.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Egypt does not generally operate a standalone UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations regime. Substance remains relevant under the arm's-length principle, beneficial-ownership analysis, treaty anti-abuse principles, the general anti-avoidance framework, permanent-establishment rules, and the ETA's power to challenge sham or artificial arrangements. A copper-scrap trading LLC should maintain genuine Egyptian management, personnel or outsourced operational capacity, premises, inventory controls, commercial decision-making, banking activity, risk assumption, and documentary evidence proportionate to its functions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion and false tax reporting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing sales, understating scrap volumes or prices, maintaining parallel books, issuing or using false invoices, omitting cash receipts, fabricating expenses, or deliberately claiming unsupported deductions or losses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Assessment of unpaid tax, additional tax, interest or statutory late-payment charges, administrative fines, and criminal prosecution. Tax-evasion offenses may carry imprisonment and fines that can be linked to the evaded tax, with enhanced consequences for aggravated or repeated conduct.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, managers, authorized signatories, accountants, and other responsible individuals may face personal criminal liability where they directed, approved, assisted, or knowingly tolerated the conduct. Civil recovery, attachment of assets, travel restrictions, and imprisonment may arise under the applicable criminal and tax procedures.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Trading copper scrap without required VAT registration, issuing invoices without actual supplies, claiming input VAT on fictitious purchases, using another taxpayer's registration, or failing to reconcile VAT returns with customs, sales, inventory, and bank records.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: VAT assessments, denial of input credits, repayment of improperly refunded tax, additional tax, administrative fines, seizure or suspension measures where available, and criminal sanctions for fraudulent invoicing or tax evasion.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Responsible directors and signatories may be prosecuted personally for intentional VAT fraud or fraudulent documentation and may face civil recovery, asset measures, travel restrictions, and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Misdescribing copper wire or scrap, undervaluing shipments, using false certificates of origin, bypassing customs controls, exporting restricted scrap without authorization, or mismatching shipping, weighbridge, invoice, and customs data.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Customs reassessment, confiscation, fines, forfeiture of goods or conveyances, suspension of customs privileges, and criminal prosecution under Egyptian customs and anti-smuggling laws.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, customs brokers, logistics personnel, and beneficial owners may incur personal criminal or civil liability where they participated in, instructed, or knowingly facilitated the violation. Asset seizure, travel restrictions, and imprisonment may apply.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unlicensed scrap dealing and environmental non-compliance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Buying, storing, processing, transporting, importing, or exporting scrap metal without required commercial, industrial, environmental, waste-management, or sectoral permits; handling hazardous contamination without controls; or operating an unauthorized yard or warehouse.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative closure, license cancellation, confiscation, environmental remediation orders, fines, compensation claims, and criminal penalties under applicable commercial, environmental, waste, and licensing legislation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and managers may be personally liable for intentional or negligent environmental and licensing breaches, including remediation costs, civil damages, administrative restrictions, and imprisonment where a criminal offense is established.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Purchasing copper from unknown suppliers, accepting unexplained cash, structuring payments, using nominee counterparties, dealing with stolen utility cable, ignoring sanctions or suspicious-activity indicators, or failing to maintain customer and supplier records.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Suspicious transaction reporting failures, account freezing, transaction blocking, confiscation, fines, and criminal prosecution under Egyptian anti-money-laundering and proceeds-of-crime legislation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, compliance officers, beneficial owners, and employees may face personal criminal liability for knowing participation, concealment, facilitation, or failure to report where legally required. Asset confiscation, travel restrictions, and imprisonment may apply.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using non-arm's-length prices for related-party copper purchases or sales, shifting profit through unsupported management fees, excessive interest, guarantees, royalties, or logistics charges, or failing to maintain required documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Primary or secondary tax adjustments, denial of deductions, withholding-tax reassessments, penalties for inaccurate returns or missing documentation, and late-payment charges.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and signatories may face personal consequences where transfer-pricing manipulation forms part of deliberate tax evasion, fraud, falsification, or concealment. Ordinary bona fide pricing disputes ordinarily create company-level tax liability rather than automatic veil piercing.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Routing dividends, interest, or royalties through a conduit entity, submitting an invalid tax-residence certificate, misrepresenting beneficial ownership, or relying on treaty relief without substance or entitlement.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty relief, withholding at domestic rates, recovery of underwithheld tax, additional tax, penalties, interest, and potential fraud or tax-evasion prosecution.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers who knowingly submit false treaty documents or approve abusive arrangements may face personal civil and criminal liability, including asset measures, travel restrictions, and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Corporate records, beneficial ownership, and AML-KYC failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to maintain accurate shareholder and beneficial-owner information, using nominee ownership to conceal control, submitting false commercial-registration information, or failing to update statutory records and tax registrations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines, registration suspension, refusal of filings, enhanced tax audits, transaction restrictions, and criminal sanctions where the conduct involves fraud, money laundering, or concealment of ownership.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managers and authorized representatives may be personally liable for false filings and intentional concealment. Civil restitution, asset attachment, travel restrictions, and imprisonment may apply depending on the offense.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Profit repatriation and foreign-exchange control risk
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing profits without approved accounts or distributable profits, disguising dividends as loans or service fees, making undocumented related-party transfers, or using informal settlement channels outside regulated banking arrangements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Invalid distribution claims, withholding-tax reassessment, banking and foreign-exchange compliance measures, fines, recovery of funds, and potential criminal exposure for fraud, money laundering, or unauthorized financial activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors approving unlawful distributions or knowingly mischaracterized transfers may face shareholder claims, creditor claims, tax liability, civil restitution, asset restrictions, travel bans, and imprisonment where criminal conduct is proven.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Offering or paying improper benefits to customs officials, licensing authorities, tax officials, procurement personnel, or public-sector counterparties to obtain clearance, permits, tax treatment, or commercial advantage.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal prosecution, imprisonment, fines, confiscation of benefits, contract cancellation, debarment, and corporate or administrative sanctions under Egyptian anti-corruption and penal laws.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Individuals who offer, authorize, arrange, or conceal bribes may face personal imprisonment, fines, confiscation, travel restrictions, and civil recovery. Corporate liability may arise through acts of representatives and responsible management.
